ar.name: Arabic
rules: Modern Standard Arabic, concise and formal.

Address: avoid gendered second-person forms (أنتَ/أنتِ and gendered imperatives such as أعِد). Use verbal nouns and the passive ("إعادة تحميل الصفحة", "تم إخفاء …"), and "يُرجى" with a verbal noun for requests ("يُرجى إعادة تحميل الصفحة").

Plurals: fill all six cases. zero may drop the number ("لا توجد تعليقات"); one is the singular and may drop it ("تعليق واحد"); two is the dual without the number ("تعليقان"); few (3–10) takes the plural ("# تعليقات"); many (11–99) the accusative singular ("# تعليقًا"); other (100 and more) the singular ("# تعليق").
Direction: the interface is right to left. Keep Latin names, DOIs, URLs and placeholders as they are; do not add direction marks.
Punctuation: Arabic comma ، semicolon ؛ and question mark ؟. Use diacritics only where they prevent a misreading (تعليقًا).

avoid.message: Avoid أنت: use verbal nouns or يُرجى.
Use Arabic punctuation (، ؟ ؛) next to Arabic text.

de.name: German
rules: Address: neither "du" nor "Sie". Use infinitives for instructions and buttons ("Seite neu laden, um …") and impersonal or passive phrasing for statements ("Die E-Mail-Adresse wird nur … gesendet"). Replace "Ihre"/"deine" with the article. Where a sentence seems to need direct address, restructure it as a noun phrase or passive.
People: name both forms ("Autorinnen und Autoren") or use neutral nouns ("Personen"); no gender star or colon.
Typography: quotation marks „…“; a spaced en dash – for the English em dash; the ellipsis character ….

avoid.message: Informal address (du/dein): use infinitives or impersonal phrasing.
Formal address (Sie/Ihr) mid-sentence: use infinitives or impersonal phrasing.

es.name: Spanish
rules: Address: prefer impersonal phrasing; buttons and menu items use the infinitive ("Volver a cargar"). Where a sentence needs address, use usted ("Recargue", "su correo"); never tú or vos.

Neutral Spanish that reads naturally in Spain and Latin America: avoid regional words (ordenador/computadora, móvil/celular, coger) and regional verb choices (añadir/agregar → "indicar" or rephrase); "correo electrónico", "Configuración".
Plurals: the many case reads like other.
People: neutral or collective nouns ("las personas", "el equipo autor", "quienes"); no @, x or e endings.
Typography: opening ¿ and ¡; quotation marks «…».

avoid.message: Use usted, never tú or vos.

fr.name: French
rules: Address: buttons, menu items and labels use the infinitive ("Recharger la page"). Full sentences that address the reader use vous ("Rechargez cette page …", "votre adresse"); never tu.
ORE is read letter by letter, so elide before it: "d'ORE", "l'extension ORE". No article before ORE otherwise ("ORE a été mis à jour").
Plurals: French "one" also covers 0, so keep # in the one case ("# commentaire", never "Un commentaire"). The many case reads like other.

Typography: narrow no-break space (U+202F) before ? ! ; and a no-break space (U+00A0) before :. Quotation marks « … » with no-break spaces inside. Replace the English em dash with a colon or a spaced en dash.
People: epicene wording ("les personnes", "l'équipe de recherche"); no point médian.

avoid.message: Use vous, never tu.
Put a narrow no-break space (U+202F) before ? ! ;
Use a no-break space, not a normal space, before ? ! ; :

hu.name: Hungarian
rules: Address: prefer impersonal phrasing. Where a sentence needs address, use the formal Ön forms without the pronoun ("Töltse újra", "e-mail-címét"); never te forms ("Töltsd újra").

Articles follow pronunciation: "az ORE", "a PubPeer", "a DOI". Acronyms and abbreviations take hyphenated suffixes ("ORE-t", "DOI-t"); other names follow the usual spelling for foreign names ("Crossrefben", "Unpaywallon"). Hyphenate compounds with a name ("PubPeer-hozzászólás", "FORRT-közösség"). Google and Microsoft products keep their official Hungarian names ("Google Táblázatok").
Plurals: the noun stays singular after a number, so one and other read the same ("# hozzászólás").
Typography: quotation marks „…”.

avoid.message: Use the formal Ön forms, never te.

ko.name: Korean
rules: Register: polite 해요체, with the honorific -세요 for requests ("새로고침하세요"), as in FLoRA for Zotero. Buttons, labels and menu items use noun forms ("저장", "새로고침", "설정 열기"). Never 반말, and keep one register throughout.
Address: leave out the subject; never 당신 or 너.
Plurals: Korean has no plural forms. Keep the one and other cases with the same text and use counters ("#개", "#건", "#편").
Spacing: standard 띄어쓰기. Latin names stay in Latin script ("PubPeer 댓글").

avoid.message: Leave out the subject; never 당신 or 너.

pt-BR.name: Brazilian Portuguese
rules: Address: você is the respectful standard; leave the pronoun out where the verb makes it clear. Requests use the third-person imperative ("Recarregue", "Adicione"); never tu.
Brazilian vocabulary and grammar: arquivo, tela, usuário, celular, Configurações; the gerund is fine ("está carregando"). 1990 spelling agreement.
Use the article with the product name: "o ORE".
Plurals: Portuguese "one" also covers 0, so keep # in the one case. The many case reads like other.

avoid.message: Use você or no pronoun, never tu.
European Portuguese word: use the Brazilian one (arquivo, tela, usuário, celular).

pt-PT.name: European Portuguese
rules: Address: avoid você, which can sound condescending in Portugal. Use the third-person verb without a pronoun ("Recarregue", "que ocultou") and "o seu"/"a sua" for possessives; never tu.

European vocabulary and grammar: ficheiro, ecrã, utilizador, telemóvel, Definições; "estar a" with the infinitive, not the gerund ("está a carregar"). Translate from the English; never adapt Brazilian Portuguese.
Use the article with the product name: "o ORE".
Plurals: the many case reads like other.

avoid.message: Avoid você: use the third-person verb without a pronoun.
Never tu in the interface.
Brazilian word: use the European one (ficheiro, ecrã, utilizador, telemóvel, Definições).
Use estar a + infinitive, not the gerund.

ro.name: Romanian
rules: Address: use the polite plural forms ("Reîncărcați", "vă", "le-ați ascuns"); never the tu forms ("Reîncarcă", "ți"). Buttons use the same polite imperative or a noun ("Setări").
Diacritics: ș and ț with comma below (U+0219, U+021B), never the cedilla forms ş ţ (U+015F, U+0163). Use â inside words and î at their start or end.
Plurals: one is 1; few is 0 and 2–19 ("# comentarii"); other is 20 and more and takes "de" ("# de comentarii").
Typography: quotation marks „…”.

avoid.message: Use ș and ț with comma below, not the cedilla forms ş ţ.
Use the polite plural forms (dumneavoastră), never tu.

zh-CN.name: Simplified Chinese (Mainland China)
rules: Concise written Chinese. Leave out the pronoun; where one is needed use 您, never 你. Polite requests start with 请.

Punctuation: full-width ，。：；？！（）and “…”; no full stop at the end of buttons and labels. Half-width digits and Latin letters, with a half-width space between them and Chinese characters ("ORE 已更新", "3 条评论").
Plurals: Chinese has no plural forms. Keep the one and other cases with the same text and use measure words (条评论, 篇论文, 项研究).
Mainland terminology and Simplified characters only (设置, 网站, 文件).

avoid.message: Use 您 or leave out the pronoun, never 你.
Use full-width punctuation (，。？！：；) next to Chinese text.

avoid.pattern: [這個們來說時會對與為發開關問題設網頁檔體]
avoid.message: Traditional character: use Simplified Chinese.
